resources.string: Protection on · %1$d app(s) filtered · %2$d app(s) cut off
Full blocking: all traffic of the cut-off apps is blocked.
Some apps are also in telemetry mode: the cut-off apps are blocked through DNS only (a connection to a hard-coded IP address can get through). For full blocking, use only the “Block everything” mode.
Tap an app to choose its mode: “Telemetry” blocks only known tracking domains, “Block everything” cuts off all its network access. Long-press an app to see its log.
First choose a mode for at least one app.
Block everything (no incoming or outgoing connection)
Google Play Services, Google Services Framework and Play Store: no telemetry and no communication, in either direction.

Google Play Services, Google Services Framework and the Play Store will have no network access at all.

Possible consequences:
• no push notifications in many apps (messaging, banking…)
• no downloads or updates from the Play Store
• “Sign in with Google”, Google Pay/Wallet, backup, Find My Device and fast location stop working
• some apps may refuse to start

You can undo this at any time with this switch.
Google services set to “Block everything”. Turn protection on to apply the block.
VPN permission denied: protection cannot start.
DNS requests and connections of all filtered apps. Tap a line to block or allow the domain.

No requests yet. Turn protection on, then use the filtered apps.
Direct connection to an IP address, blocked because the app is in “Block everything” mode.

%1$d built-in telemetry domains (Firebase, Google Analytics, AppsFlyer, Adjust, Sentry, Crashlytics, Mixpanel…). Their subdomains are blocked too.
